newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl turns screws on FDP partners over tax-paper.
newsitem.headline: Kohl turns screws on FDP partners over tax-paper.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl threatened junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) on Tuesday with a grand coalition embracing opposition parties if the FDP failed to drop opposition to tax increases, a newspaper reported.
Die Welt daily reported that Kohl made the threat at a closed-door emergency coalition meeting in Bonn.
The liberal FDP, which has depicted itself as party of low taxes, vehemently opposes any tax increases to help Bonn fill gaping budget holes and qualify for Europe's single currency.
The Handlesblatt business daily said Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) had proposed raising taxes on petrol, tobacco and alcohol at the meeting on Tuesday.
Leading FDP member Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel told the Berliner Tageszeitung he did not think the current crisis would lead to a break up of the coalition.

"I have sat on the cabinet for six and a half years... and I have experienced many a difficult situation in the coalition. Yes, we have a serious situation at the moment, but the situation can be overcome," he said in an interview released ahead of publication on Wednesday.
